## Recall · Lecture 10

a) What is the resolution of Full HD?
b) Which codec plays on almost every phone?
c) A fast chase looks like blocks. What is too low?

::: {.answer}
a) 1920 × 1080
b) H.264
c) the bitrate
:::

## Activity 1 · Project and clips · 15 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A new project needs its resolution and frame rate first, and imported clips appear in the media pool.
- **Do it:** Make a project of 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps. Import three clips and write the resolution, frame rate and codec of each. Which clip does not match?
- Your product is a table of three clips.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/workflow.png)
:::
::::

## Check 1 · Project and clips

What does a typical table of the clips show?

::: {.reveal}
1. A clip of 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps with H.264 matches the project.
2. A tall phone clip of 1080 × 1920 does not match, so it must be cropped, never stretched.
3. A clip at 60 fps has twice the frame rate of the project.
:::

## Activity 2 · Two exports · 18 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A store trailer is an MP4 with H.264, at the resolution and frame rate of the project.
- **Do it:** Put the clips on the timeline. Export yourname-teaser-v1.mp4, then a second file with a much lower bitrate. Compare the sizes and the moving parts.
- Your product is two files and one sentence.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/export-settings.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · Two exports

What do the two exports show?

::: {.reveal}
1. The first file looks clean and is a few MB for 10 to 20 seconds.
2. The low-bitrate file is much smaller, but its fast moving parts show blocks.
3. A higher bitrate gives a better picture and a bigger file.
4. The producer gets the MP4, never the project file.
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can make a project with the right settings and read the settings of a clip.
- You can export a video for a target and see what the bitrate changes.
